intro: A home in Charlotte, a townhouse in Raleigh and a coastal property near Wilmington can have very different monthly ownership costs, even when their purchase prices are identical. Property taxes, insurance requirements and association fees can significantly influence affordability.

Our free North Carolina mortgage calculator helps you estimate your monthly housing expenses before purchasing a property. Enter your home price, down payment, interest rate and loan term, then include property taxes, homeowners insurance and other applicable costs to establish a realistic budget.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in North Carolina?

blocks.markdown:
A $290,000 North Carolina home purchased with a 20% down payment and financed through a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed annual interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $1,390.96.

Including illustrative property taxes and insurance produces the following estimate.
This example assumes no private mortgage insurance or association fees. Taxes, insurance premiums and the interest rate are illustrative rather than current statewide averages.

sections.heading: Understanding the North Carolina Housing Market

blocks.markdown:
North Carolina offers housing opportunities across metropolitan neighborhoods, university communities, mountain towns and coastal regions.

According to the [US Census Bureau's North Carolina housing statistics](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/NC/HSG860224), the median value of owner-occupied housing was $288,900 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Median selected monthly ownership costs among homeowners with mortgages were $1,631, while the homeownership rate was 66.6%.

These historical statistics provide useful context but do not represent current mortgage offers or property asking prices.

Homes near employment centers in Charlotte, Raleigh and Durham may have different purchase prices from properties in smaller communities. Coastal homes can also involve additional insurance expenses.

Research recent comparable property sales and investigate recurring ownership costs before selecting a purchase price for the calculator.

sections.heading: How to Use the North Carolina Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Start by entering the property's expected purchase price and your available down payment.

Select your repayment period and enter the annual interest rate quoted by your lender. If you have not received a quote, consult [Freddie Mac's mortgage market survey](https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms) for a national reference.

Next, include annual property taxes, homeowners insurance premiums and monthly association fees.

Add private mortgage insurance if your conventional financing requires it.

Review your estimated monthly housing payment and adjust individual inputs to compare financing arrangements.

The amortization schedule shows how much of each mortgage payment goes toward interest and reducing your outstanding balance.

Use our national Mortgage Calculator to compare borrowing scenarios outside North Carolina.

sections.heading: How North Carolina Property Taxes Affect Your Mortgage

blocks.markdown:
North Carolina real estate taxes depend on property valuations and applicable local tax rates.

County assessors establish property values, while counties, municipalities and certain special districts determine the tax rates used to fund local services.

The property's assessed value may differ from its current purchase price, particularly when local real estate prices have changed since the last countywide reappraisal.

### North Carolina property reappraisals

According to the [North Carolina Department of Revenue](https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/property-tax/types-property-be-taxed), counties must conduct real property reappraisals at least once every eight years.

Some counties conduct reappraisals more frequently, including on four-year cycles.

A reappraisal can increase or decrease the assessed value used for taxation. However, a higher assessed value does not necessarily result in an identical percentage increase in the final tax bill because local tax rates may also change.

Ask your county assessor about upcoming reappraisals before relying on a property's existing tax bill.

### North Carolina property tax calculation example

Suppose a home has an assessed value of $290,000 and is subject to the following hypothetical tax rates.

The estimated annual property tax would be:

$290,000 ÷ 100 × $0.93 = $2,697

This represents approximately $224.75 per month.

Actual taxes depend on your property's jurisdiction, assessment and applicable exemptions or additional charges.

### Property tax exemptions and relief

North Carolina offers property tax relief to certain eligible homeowners, including qualifying older residents, people with permanent disabilities and disabled veterans.

The elderly or disabled exclusion generally removes the greater of $25,000 or 50% of the qualifying permanent residence's appraised value from taxation.

Income, ownership and residency requirements apply.

Review the [North Carolina Department of Revenue's property tax resources](https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/property-tax) and contact your county assessor to investigate eligibility.

Do not automatically apply these exemptions to every homeowner.

North Carolina properties face different environmental risks depending on their location.

Coastal communities may experience hurricanes and storm surge, while inland and mountain regions can experience flooding, severe storms and other weather-related damage.

Obtain property-specific insurance quotes before completing your purchase.

### Coastal windstorm and hail insurance

The [North Carolina Department of Insurance](https://www.ncdoi.gov/consumers/homeowners-insurance/windstorm-and-hail) explains that some homeowners policies exclude windstorm and hail coverage.

Homeowners in eligible coastal areas may need separate coverage through the North Carolina Insurance Underwriting Association or another suitable insurer.

Separate windstorm policies may also have their own deductibles.

For example, a 2% deductible calculated against $300,000 in dwelling coverage would represent $6,000 in potential out-of-pocket expenses for an applicable covered claim.

### Flood insurance

Standard homeowners insurance generally excludes flooding. This matters for both coastal communities and inland properties near rivers or flood-prone areas.

Investigate your property's flood exposure using the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home).

Add the annual cost of separate flood and windstorm policies to your mortgage estimate when applicable.

Avoid counting coverage twice if your primary homeowners policy already includes it.
The following estimates assume a 20% down payment, a 6% fixed annual interest rate and a 30-year mortgage.

These figures exclude taxes, homeowners insurance, PMI and association fees.

Compare complete housing payments rather than principal and interest alone.

The North Carolina Housing Finance Agency offers mortgage financing and purchase assistance through participating lenders.

### NC Home Advantage Mortgage

The [NC Home Advantage Mortgage program](https://nchfa.com/home-buyers/buy-home/nc-home-advantage-mortgage) serves qualifying first-time and repeat homebuyers.

Eligible borrowers may receive down payment assistance of up to 3% of their mortgage amount.

For example, 3% assistance on a qualifying $232,000 mortgage would amount to $6,960.

Following the June 2026 program update, the published statewide income limit increased to $158,000, while the purchase price limit increased to $525,000.

Additional credit, occupancy, financing and property requirements apply.

### NC 1st Home Advantage Down Payment

Eligible first-time buyers and military veterans may qualify for $15,000 in down payment assistance through the NC 1st Home Advantage option.

The assistance is conditional financing rather than an immediate unconditional grant.

Under the agency's published forgiveness schedule, 20% is forgiven annually at the end of years 11 through 15. Selling, refinancing or transferring the property before full forgiveness can trigger repayment obligations.

Compare the complete costs of each financing arrangement and confirm current eligibility with a participating lender.

sections.heading: Comparing Mortgage Terms in North Carolina

blocks.markdown:
A shorter mortgage term can reduce your lifetime interest expenses but requires a larger monthly payment.

For example, borrowing $232,000 at 6% over 30 years requires approximately $1,390.96 monthly in principal and interest.

Repaying the same loan over 15 years at the same interest rate would require approximately $1,957.54 monthly.

Use the amortization schedule to compare interest savings and determine whether the higher monthly commitment fits your budget.

sections.heading: Additional Costs of Owning a North Carolina Home

blocks.markdown:
Homebuyers should investigate expenses beyond their regular mortgage payments.

Properties in managed developments may have association dues, special assessments and community maintenance obligations.

Coastal homes can require additional exterior maintenance, while rural properties may involve private wells, septic systems and access roads.

Use our [North Carolina Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/north-carolina-paycheck-calculator/) to estimate after-tax earnings and our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) to evaluate existing financial obligations.

Compare lender offers using the [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's Loan Estimate guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/).

Maintain sufficient savings for closing costs, insurance deductibles and unexpected repairs.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $290,000 North Carolina home?

With 20% down, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year mortgage, monthly principal and interest would be approximately $1,390.96. Property taxes, insurance and applicable fees increase the total housing payment.

### How are North Carolina property taxes calculated?

Property taxes generally depend on the county's assessed property value and applicable local tax rates. Counties, municipalities and special taxing districts may contribute to the final tax bill.

### Does North Carolina offer $15,000 in down payment assistance?

Yes. Eligible first-time homebuyers and military veterans may qualify for $15,000 through the NC 1st Home Advantage Down Payment program. Income, credit, property and forgiveness requirements apply.

Replace illustrative expenses with accurate local property taxes and insurance quotes. Understanding your complete housing costs can help you choose a property that supports sustainable homeownership.
